title: Daruma Otoshi
summary: A traditional Japanese skill toy: a tower of coloured wooden discs with a round painted head on top. Using a small wooden mallet you knock the discs out one at a time from the side, so that the rest drop straight down and the head ends up on the base.
howToPlay: Press the disc you want to remove, pull the mallet back and let go. Aim for the marked window on the strength gauge.
A blow that is too soft only shakes the tower; one that is too hard drags the next disc out as well.
Work from the bottom up and keep the wobble low until the head comes down.
rules: A clean blow sends one disc out and scores 1; the wobble settles a little.
A soft blow or a hard blow adds to the wobble; when the wobble is full the tower falls and the round ends.
Bringing the head down to the base with the tower still standing scores a bonus of 3.
Each round gives eight blows; three rounds make a game. Discs higher up need a slightly firmer blow.
heritageNote: A children's game of patience and a steady hand from Japan, played with a small mallet and a tower of discs. The toy is still made in wood and played at home and at gatherings.
